Seminar Title:

Convergence- and Diffraction-Aware Cross-Band Ray Tracing of FR1, FR3, and FR2: From Propagation to MIMO and Network Coverage

Seminar Type:

Registration Seminar

Department:

Electronics and Communication Engineering

Speaker Name:

Priyanka Priyadarsinee ( Rollno : 524ec1018)

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

EC303- Seminar Room, ECE Department

Date and Time:

16 Nov 2026 05:30 P.M

Contact:

Sadananda Behera

Abstract:

The upper mid-band (FR3, about 6&ndash24 GHz) is a key candidate band for 6G,&nbspsince it offers higher data rates than FR1 and lower path loss, less blockage and&nbspbetter coverage than FR2. In non-line-of-sight (NLOS) conditions, coverage depends on diffraction, reflection, and scattering. Diffraction loss at building edges&nbsprises quickly with frequency, so its contribution is expected to change strongly from&nbspband to band. We isolate its effect with site-specific ray tracing (Sionna RT) on an&nbspOpenStreetMap campus environment, using paired runs with diffraction on and off&nbspat 3.5, 10, 15, 28 and 36 GHz. Six fixed base stations (BS 8&times8 UPA) serve 150 fixed&nbspoutdoor users (UE 1 &times 4 ULA), with the same maximum interaction depth in every&nbsprun. The comparison covers serving-BS association, received power, LOS-to-NLOS&nbsppower ratio, RMS delay spread and path count, and then SINR and rate coverage.&nbspDiffraction raises the mean number of resolved paths of NLOS links, but gives a&nbspreceived-power gain to only a few users the maximum finite gain falls from 50.4&nbspdB at 3.5 GHz to 44.4 dB at 36 GHz. At the 0 dB SINR target it rescues only&nbsp2.2&ndash4.9% of NLOS users. Diffraction therefore mainly reshapes the NLOS channel&nbspand changes coverage for a small set of shadowed users, with an effect that weakens&nbspas the frequency increases.
